subject: SLA runbook & deployment decision follow-up

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: SLA runbook & deployment decision follow-up

Hi Sanjay — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposal so we can converge on the deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity) given FastRetail's latency and throughput targets.

Call notes (from your side):
- P95 latency target: <= 75 ms for search/sku-lookup flows, 95% of traffic is read-only inference.
- Sustained throughput: ~150 qps with predictable diurnal peaks to 300 qps for 20-45 minutes.
- Bursts: occasional flash sales with short spikes to ~800 qps for 3–10 minutes (behind CDN).
- Data residency: All inference logs must stay in US; no PII stored.

Primary ask: which deployment path gives predictable p95 while keeping unit economics tolerable? You asked for a short runbook + a top-line capacity estimate for Dedicated vs hosted pilot.

Proposed next steps (high level):
1) We’ll share an SLA-runbook v1 (attached) that maps breakpoints to recommendation (pilot on Hosted vs commit to Dedicated).
2) Quick Dedicated estimate for FR volumes (spreadsheet attached).
3) Two-week hosted pilot with synthetic load to validate p95 at your representative qps. If pilot fails p95 at target, we move to Dedicated reservation and define canary windows.

I’ve cc'd the ops folks who can quote Dedicated pool sizing and run the pilot. Please confirm the representative traffic sample you want us to use (e.g., 60% lightweight token-only prompts, 40% multi-turn with 512-token context).

Best,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook summary), capacity-estimate-fr-2026.xlsx (top-line sizing)

Thanks, Priyom — that looks good. A few clarifications:
- The traffic mix is closer to what you suggested: ~65% short lookups (10–30 tokens), ~35% multi-turn (~200–512 tokens).
- For the flashes, CDN will front most requests but the app will still fan out to Redwood; we need graceful degradation if p95 slips.
- Budget: procurement wants a 90-day pilot on Hosted before any long-term reservation. If Dedicated is required, they need a 12-month committed quote and a quick ROI calc.

Could you include 1) a Hosted pilot SLO we can sign up to, 2) a ping-pong test pattern we can run to reproduce the spikes, and 3) a top-line monthly cost compare for Hosted vs a Dedicated reserve that covers sustained 150 qps + burst headroom?

Appreciate it — cc'd Procurement so they see the ask.

— Sanjay
Director, Engineering
FastRetail
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA runbook & deployment decision follow-up

Looping in recommended breakpoints and a concise technical rationale so Priyom can send a single-run recommendation to FastRetail. Notes below are internal.

Quick decision matrix (ops-friendly):
- If sustained qps <= 200 and p95 target >= 50–100ms: Hosted API pilot first. Rationale: autoscaling and prefix/KV caching will reduce tail for mostly read-heavy traffic; lower friction for procurement.
- If sustained qps in 200–400 or if burst-to-sustained ratio > 2x and p95 <= 75ms: Recommend Dedicated with autoscale policy + burst pool. Rationale: Dedicated gives predictable GPU assignment to reduce p95 variance under sustained high utilization.
- If bursts > 700 qps persist beyond 5–10 minutes and strict p95 <= 75ms required: Dedicated reserved capacity with canary routing and optional warm-up pools.

Technical tradeoffs to include in runbook:
- Batching improves throughput but increases median latency; continuous batching parameters must be tuned per flow.
- KV/prefix caching can shave 20–50% of token work for heavy repeatable prefixes (search queries).
- Quantization or smaller family model variants help cost but may introduce quality regressions — include eval checks in pilot.

Pilot runbook (2-week Hosted pilot recommended):
1) Day 0–2: Onboard keys, set up request tracing and token-level cost breakdown in Console.
2) Day 3–5: Synthetic spike test (ping-pong pattern + CDN-introduced fanout) to reproduce flash loads.
3) Day 6–10: Measure p50/p95/p99 across targeted endpoints with real sample traffic.
4) Day 11–14: If p95 > 75ms under representative sustained qps, switch to Dedicated sizing (pre-approved sizing path below) and schedule a canary.

Dedicated sizing (top-line):
- For 150 sustained qps with 65/35 mix and average tokens per request ~120: estimate 3–4 x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent) with continuous batching and a 1.5x burst pool for short spikes. Exact #s in the attached spreadsheet.

Action items (internal):
- Ben: Produce a top-line Dedicated vs Hosted cost delta and monthly commitment quote (due EOD 10/06).
- Rachel: Prep the Hosted pilot SLO language and the synthetic spike script (due 10/06).
- Priyom: Send consolidated note to Sanjay with attachments and ask for sample traffic dump.

Marissa
Head of Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLA runbook & deployment decision follow-up

Sanjay — attaching the SLA-runbook v1 and a top-line capacity/cost estimate (both attached). Short summary and next steps below.

Short recommendation:
- Start with a 14-day Hosted pilot under our Hosted SLO (we’ll guarantee priority routing and monitoring for the pilot window). This lets us validate p95 at your sample mix with the least procurement friction.
- If p95 > 75ms during sustained 150 qps window, Redwood recommends moving to Dedicated reserved capacity sized per the attached workbook. We’ll define a 2-day canary with warm-up pool before full cutover.

What we need from FastRetail to begin the pilot:
1) Representative traffic sample (or 48 hours of logs) — format: gzipped ndjson of requests (timestamps, path, token_count).
2) Confirmation you accept the Hosted pilot SLO below (one-paragraph acceptance).
3) Procurement contact to sign the 14-day pilot agreement (we can do via e-sign).

Pilot SLO (summary):
- Redwood will maintain service availability and priority routing for pilot endpoints; we measure p95 at the edge. If p95 exceeds 75ms for >5m sustained at target qps, Redwood will present Dedicated sizing and schedule a canary. Pilot costs billed at standard Hosted rates; we will provide a one-time credit if migration to Dedicated is required due to infra limitations.

Next steps & owners:
- Sanjay: Send sample traffic or confirm we should use synthetic pattern (by 10/07).
- Procurement: Confirm pilot signatory and PO path (by 10/09).
- Ben: Attach Dedicated quote and monthly commitment breakdown (on the spreadsheet).

Thanks — will follow up with a short DocuSign link once you confirm pilot acceptance.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
